chapters.1.lds: The selected lesson studies faithful responses and waiting through Mary, Elizabeth, and Zacharias. How does Mary’s song connect her own blessing with hungry and powerful people?
chapters.1.summary: Luke says he has written an orderly account from eyewitness reports. An angel tells the old priest Zacharias that his wife will bear a son, John. Zacharias doubts and is made unable to speak. Gabriel tells Mary she will bear a son called the Son of the Most High. Mary visits Elizabeth, who blesses her. Mary sings that God has looked on her low position. John is born, and Zacharias speaks again. He praises God for raising up a savior.
chapters.2.lds: Why does Simeon place pain beside the promise of light?
chapters.2.summary: Caesar Augustus orders a registration, and Joseph and Mary travel to Bethlehem. Mary gives birth and lays her son in a feeding trough. Angels announce the birth to shepherds in the fields. The shepherds find the child and tell what they heard. In the temple old Simeon takes the child in his arms. He calls him a light for the nations and warns Mary of sorrow. The prophetess Anna gives thanks. At twelve, Jesus stays behind in the temple among the teachers.
chapters.3.lds: The selected lesson reads changed conduct as evidence of repentance. How do John’s different answers address each group’s use of resources or power?
chapters.3.summary: In the fifteenth year of Tiberius, John preaches a baptism of repentance. He warns the crowds not to rely on descent from Abraham. The people ask what they should do. He tells them to share coats and food. Tax collectors must collect no more than is due. Soldiers must not extort money. John says one mightier than he is coming. Jesus is baptized, and Luke traces his family line back to Adam.
chapters.4.lds: Why do the examples of Elijah and Elisha anger the hometown listeners?
chapters.4.summary: Jesus is tested by the devil in the desert for forty days. He returns to Galilee and teaches in the synagogues. In Nazareth he reads from Isaiah about good news for the poor. He says the Scripture is fulfilled that day. The people speak well of him at first. He reminds them that Elijah helped a foreign widow and Elisha a Syrian. They are furious and try to throw him off a cliff. He goes on to Capernaum and heals many.
chapters.5.lds: How does the physician comparison explain the company at Levi’s meal?
chapters.5.summary: Jesus teaches from Simon’s boat and tells him to let down the nets. They catch so many fish that the nets begin to break. Simon, James, and John leave everything and follow him. He heals a man with a skin disease and a paralyzed man. He calls Levi, a tax collector, who leaves his booth. Levi gives a great feast with many tax collectors. Pharisees complain about the company. Jesus says he came to call sinners to repentance.
chapters.6.lds: Why does love for enemies go beyond exchanging equal favors?
chapters.6.summary: Jesus is challenged twice about the Sabbath. He spends a night in prayer and chooses twelve apostles. He teaches a great crowd on level ground. He blesses the poor and the hungry and warns the rich. He tells them to love their enemies and do good to those who hate them. They should lend and expect nothing back. They should not judge, and they should forgive. The one who hears and acts builds on rock.
chapters.7.lds: What does Simon fail to see before Jesus compares their acts of welcome?
chapters.7.summary: Jesus heals a Roman officer’s servant from a distance. At Nain he raises a widow’s only son. John the Baptist sends to ask whether Jesus is the one to come. A Pharisee named Simon invites Jesus to dinner. A woman known as a sinner weeps over his feet and anoints them. Simon thinks a prophet would know what she is. Jesus tells of two debtors forgiven different amounts. He tells the woman that her sins are forgiven.
chapters.8.lds: How does the family saying join hearing with doing?
chapters.8.summary: Jesus travels with the twelve and with women who support them from their own means. He tells of a farmer sowing seed on four soils. His mother and brothers cannot reach him through the crowd. He says his family are those who hear God’s word and do it. He calms a storm on the lake. He frees a man from many demons. A woman with long bleeding is healed. He raises the daughter of Jairus.
chapters.9.lds: Why does Jesus reject the disciples’ proposed fire?
chapters.9.summary: Jesus sends the twelve to preach and heal, and he feeds five thousand. Peter says he is the Christ of God. Jesus says he must suffer and that followers must take up their cross daily. He is changed in appearance on a mountain. The disciples argue over who is greatest. Jesus sets his face to go to Jerusalem. A Samaritan village refuses him. James and John want to call down fire, and he rebukes them.
chapters.10.lds: The selected lesson connects neighbor love with the Samaritan’s practical care. How does the final neighbor question change the lawyer’s original question?
chapters.10.summary: Jesus sends seventy others ahead of him in pairs. They return with joy at what they have done. A lawyer asks what he must do to inherit eternal life. He agrees that the law says to love God and neighbor. He then asks who his neighbor is. Jesus tells of a man beaten by robbers and left half dead. A priest and a Levite pass by, and a Samaritan cares for him. Jesus then visits Martha and Mary.
chapters.11.lds: What connects clean surfaces with neglected justice in the meal dispute?
chapters.11.summary: Jesus teaches his disciples a prayer and tells them to keep asking. Some say he drives out demons by their ruler. He says a divided kingdom falls. He warns that this generation seeks a sign. A Pharisee invites him to a meal and is surprised he does not wash. Jesus says they clean the outside of the cup. They tithe herbs and pass over justice and God’s love. He says the lawyers load people with burdens.
chapters.12.lds: How does the returning master’s service change expectations about power?
chapters.12.summary: Jesus warns a great crowd against hypocrisy and fear of people. A man asks him to settle an inheritance. He tells of a rich man who built bigger barns and died that night. He tells his disciples not to worry about food or clothes. They should sell what they have and give to the poor. They should be like servants waiting for their master. Much is required of the one given much. He says he has come to bring division.
chapters.13.lds: Why does Jesus reject greater guilt as the explanation for the victims’ deaths?
chapters.13.summary: People tell Jesus about Galileans whom Pilate killed. He asks whether they were worse sinners than others. He says no, and that everyone must repent. He tells of a fig tree given one more year. On a Sabbath he heals a woman bent over for eighteen years. The synagogue ruler objects. Jesus says she is a daughter of Abraham and should be set free. He weeps over Jerusalem, which kills the prophets.
chapters.14.lds: How does inviting people unable to repay challenge the host’s expectations?
chapters.14.summary: Jesus eats at a leading Pharisee’s house on the Sabbath and heals a man there. He sees guests choosing the best seats. He tells them to take the lowest place. He tells his host to invite the poor, the crippled, the lame, and the blind. He tells of a great banquet whose invited guests make excuses. The host fills his house from the streets and lanes. Jesus tells the crowds to count the cost of following him. Salt that loses its taste is thrown out.
chapters.15.lds: Why does the story end with the father’s appeal rather than the older son’s decision?
chapters.15.summary: Tax collectors and sinners gather to hear Jesus, and the Pharisees grumble. He tells of a shepherd who finds one lost sheep. He tells of a woman who finds one lost coin. He tells of a man with two sons. The younger wastes his share and comes home hungry. The father runs to him and holds a feast. The older son is angry and will not go in. The father comes out and pleads with him.
chapters.16.lds: Why does Abraham point the brothers toward words they already have?
chapters.16.summary: Jesus tells of a dishonest manager who reduces debts to win friends. He says no servant can serve two masters. The Pharisees, who love money, scoff. He tells of a rich man who feasted every day. A poor man named Lazarus lay at his gate covered with sores. Both die, and Lazarus is comforted at Abraham’s side. The rich man asks that Lazarus warn his brothers. Abraham says they have Moses and the prophets.
chapters.17.lds: Why does Jesus identify the returning man as a foreigner?
chapters.17.summary: Jesus warns against causing others to stumble and tells his disciples to forgive. A servant does not expect thanks for doing his duty. Between Samaria and Galilee ten men with a skin disease cry out for mercy. Jesus tells them to show themselves to the priests. They are healed as they go. One returns, praises God, and thanks Jesus, and he is a Samaritan. The Pharisees ask when God’s Kingdom will come. Jesus says it will come like lightning.
chapters.18.lds: The selected lesson teaches trust in God’s mercy rather than condemning others through self-praise. How does the tax collector’s prayer differ from the Pharisee’s comparisons?
chapters.18.summary: Jesus tells of a widow who keeps asking an unjust judge for justice. He tells of two men who pray in the temple. A Pharisee thanks God that he is not like other people. A tax collector asks only for mercy. People bring infants, and Jesus welcomes them. A rich ruler asks about eternal life and leaves sad. Jesus foretells his death again. Near Jericho he gives sight to a blind beggar.
chapters.19.lds: How do praise and tears coexist at the approach to Jerusalem?
chapters.19.summary: In Jericho a rich tax collector named Zacchaeus climbs a tree to see Jesus. Jesus stays at his house, and Zacchaeus promises to repay those he cheated. Jesus tells of servants entrusted with money while their master is away. He rides a colt toward Jerusalem. The disciples praise God loudly. As the city comes into view, he weeps over it. He says it did not know what would bring peace. He drives the sellers from the temple and teaches there daily.
chapters.20.lds: Whom does Luke name as the immediate targets of the vineyard story?
chapters.20.summary: The chief priests and scribes ask Jesus by what authority he acts. He asks them about John’s baptism, and they will not answer. He tells of tenants who beat the owner’s servants and kill his son. The leaders know the story is about them. They send spies to trap him with a question about taxes. Sadducees ask about the resurrection. He asks how the Christ can be David’s son. He warns the people about scribes who devour widows’ houses.
chapters.21.lds: Why does the warning about false timing claims follow the question about signs?
chapters.21.summary: Jesus sees a poor widow put two small coins in the treasury. Some admire the temple’s fine stones and gifts. He says not one stone will be left on another. They ask when and what the sign will be. He warns them not to follow those who say the time is near. Wars and disturbances must come, and the end is not yet. Jerusalem will be surrounded by armies. He tells them to stay alert and pray.
chapters.22.lds: How does Jesus’ service answer the disciples’ rank dispute?
chapters.22.summary: Judas agrees with the chief priests to hand Jesus over. Jesus eats the Passover with the apostles and gives the bread and the cup. He says one at the table will betray him. The apostles then argue about who is greatest. He says he is among them as one who serves. He prays on the Mount of Olives in anguish. He is arrested, and Peter denies him three times. The council asks whether he is the Son of God.
chapters.23.lds: How do Pilate’s decisions differ from his repeated announcements?
chapters.23.summary: The council brings Jesus to Pilate and accuses him of stirring up the nation. Pilate finds no basis for a charge and sends him to Herod. Herod mocks him and sends him back. Pilate says three times that Jesus has done nothing deserving death. The crowd demands Barabbas. Pilate grants their demand. Jesus is crucified and prays for those who do it. One criminal asks to be remembered, and Jesus dies.
chapters.24.lds: The selected lesson teaches resurrection through the Gospel accounts. How do remembered words, explained Scripture, and shared food shape recognition?
chapters.24.summary: Women find the tomb empty, and two men in shining clothes say Jesus has risen. The apostles think their report is nonsense. Two disciples walk to Emmaus, and a stranger joins them. They tell him their hopes have been crushed. He explains the Scriptures about the Christ. At supper he breaks bread, and they know him. He appears to the group in Jerusalem and eats fish. He blesses them and is carried up to heaven.
